A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Next Visual Granularity Generation. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support comparison, including matching analyses relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original NVG ImageNet generation results, tokenizer reconstruction results, ablations, and controlled-generation examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds inference-cost measurements and qualitative analyses of difficult cases and competing generators.

M1.justification: The construction and generation algorithms, architectures, losses, structure embeddings, and sampling procedures are retained. The corrected residual expression agrees with the operation already described and illustrated in v1; it does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet for class-conditional generation and reconstruction, retaining geometric/reference structure guidance and class-transfer examples. The new difficult-case and comparative image panels examine outputs within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: The original quantitative comparator sets are unchanged. v2 adds qualitative comparisons with SiT-X, IBQ-XXL, and VAR-d24, plus computational comparisons with SiT-X, IBQ-XL, and VAR-d16/d20/d24. These extend evaluated comparisons using methods already represented in v1.

E3.justification: Appendix B.5 introduces runtime and memory evaluation covering latent generation and final decoding, with stated common hardware/software/datatype/CFG conditions, VAR KV caching, and a fixed-structure NVG control. Existing training, sampling, reconstruction, and ablation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands supplementary analysis through difficult-structure and small/multiple-object case studies in Figure 7 and computational-cost decomposition with and without structure generation in Appendix B.5. The original ablations and stage-wise variation analysis are retained in Appendices B.2 and B.4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the experimental results. The new runtime and memory table likewise reports point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: All original generation, reconstruction, and ablation table values are unchanged. Table 4 adds a substantial computational comparison: NVG-d24 reports 1.122031 seconds and 3471 MiB, versus VAR-d24's 0.159784 seconds and 5539 MiB. Figures 7, 9, and 10 also add difficult-case and comparative qualitative results.

T1.justification: Section 2.2.2 corrects the residual expression from x - f_c(x_i) to f_c(x_i) - x_i, resolving its inconsistency with the stated predicted-final-minus-current-canvas operation. The numbered equations and mathematical constructions otherwise remain unchanged; no new proofs or theorems appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: structured visual granularity, explicit structure control, coarse-to-fine generation, model scaling, and the same FID comparisons with VAR. Added analyses support and qualify these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of generation with ambiguous structures and imbalanced regions, and proposes more flexible clustering. Appendix B.5 explicitly acknowledges that structure generation makes full NVG slower than VAR and explains its lower memory consumption through the absence of KV caching.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promised code/model release with statements that training and inference code and models are available. Existing implementation and hyperparameter disclosures are retained, but v1's V100/A100 hardware acknowledgment is removed; the new timing comparison does not identify its specific hardware/software configuration.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. Changes such as updated publication years, venues, and the DART title identify the same works. The detailed related-work discussion moves from Section 4 to Appendix C.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: ablations, stage-wise variation, and detailed related work move into appendices, while the main analysis emphasizes difficult cases. The conclusion incorporates limitations and discussion, and reproducibility and LLM-use statements are added, alongside smaller language and header edits.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is redrawn into pipeline and prediction-processing panels. v2 adds the difficult-case Figure 7, comparative image grids in Figures 9–10, and inference-cost Table 4. The original stage-wise Figure 7 becomes appendix Figure 8, and the retained ablation table moves to the appendix.

improvement.justification: The corrected residual expression and redesigned Figure 4 improve explanatory correctness. New case studies and measured latency/memory tradeoffs make the method easier to assess, and release information becomes more concrete. These gains improve the paper without materially changing its central empirical case. The added robustness evidence remains qualitative, timing configuration is underspecified, and the earlier hardware disclosure is lost.
